findings.title: Dependency section resolves function/class endpoints with no stated mechanism, against the read discipline
findings.description:
Section 6 says function- and class-level edge endpoints are "resolved to their owning file's layer rather than dropped". Three problems:

- **Read discipline:** the architecture says function- and class-level nodes are not read, and this design's own criterion 9 (line 333) says "no function- or class-level node is read". The design does not say how an owner is found without reading those nodes (`contains` edges, or parsing the type-prefixed id).
- **Internal contradiction:** the same paragraph scopes the section to inter-layer `imports` and `depends_on`, then says a `calls` edge between functions "still counts as an inter-layer signal".
- **Unmeasured:** the Verified graph facts table has no count of edges with function/class endpoints and no check that owner resolution succeeds. Every other decision rests on a measurement.

The lighter option meets the slice plan's "dependency observations traceable to edge data": restrict section 6 to `imports`/`depends_on` edges whose endpoints are both file-level, and report the count of excluded edges. If the roll-up is kept, specify the jq resolution path and the handling of unresolved endpoints, and reword criterion 9.

findings.title: File-level selector is self-contradictory and inverts the architecture's allow-list
Closing observations are an unmarked inference channel
findings.description:
Each section carries a closing sentence that "reads a pattern out of the data", exempt from `[INFERRED]` on a "mechanical" derivability test. The design's own example fails that test: "complexity concentrates in the seams where squadron meets an external SDK" is not derivable from a table of paths and tiers. It is a claim from indirect evidence, which is how 361 defines `[INFERRED]`.

This contradicts "the fallback column has no third option" (lines 186-189) and the fact/inference separation the design says it adopts. Closing observations also have no row in the mapping table and no success criterion. Criterion 8 (`grep -c 'INFERRED'` returns 0) measures the marker's absence, not inference's absence.

Cut closing observations; nothing in the slice plan requires them. Alternatively, mark them `[INFERRED]` and drop the zero-marker criterion.

findings.title: Mapping drops `tour[].nodeIds`, the field the plan and architecture name as the signal
findings.description:
Row 5 sources reading order from `order`, `title` and `description` only. That leaves two requirements unmet:

- The slice plan assigns 362 "`tour[]` ordering as the signal for which components matter most". Without `nodeIds`, a step names no components.
- The architecture's concept table gives "`tour[]` node ordering" as the field for Solution Approach. This design promises 363 that "layers and tour feed Solution Approach" from a mapping reused verbatim (lines 36, 299-301).

361's read list already included `tour[]` order/title/nodeIds. Add `nodeIds`, resolved to `filePath`, to row 5.

findings.title: Fallback column covers whole-section absence only
findings.description:
The slice plan makes "what fallback when a field is absent" the core deliverable, and the table is declared binding. Only row 1 handles a missing subfield. The rest leave partial absence open:

- **Row 2:** "preflight rejects empty `layers`" says nothing about a layer missing `description`.
- **Row 4:** nothing covers some nodes lacking `complexity`, which 361's design named as the likely real gap. Nothing covers a graph where no node is in the top tier.
- **Row 6:** "preflight rejects empty `edges`" does not cover zero inter-layer edges or an absent `weight`. "Ties by `weight`" does not say how a per-edge weight aggregates to a layer pair.

A renamed `weight` or a partly missing `complexity` would produce a thinner document with no marker. State the per-field fallback in each row.

findings.title: The reuse decision misdescribes the template it rejects
findings.description:
The design calls the reference document's template a "ten-part structure (identity, architecture, build/test/deploy, code quality, security, performance, operations, and so on)". The document has eight sections:

1. Identity & Stack
2. Architecture
3. Build, Test & Deploy
4. Code Quality & Defects
5. Issue Tracker & Project Health
6. AI Agent Integration
7. Risks & Recommendations
8. Deep-Dive Plan

It has no security, performance or operations sections. The conclusion (do not adopt the template) still holds, since sections 3-5 have no graph backing. But this is the recorded resolution of a parent open question, and criterion 7 carries it into the skill text. Correct the description. Also note the overlaps it misses: "files to read first" and "where the complexity lives" map to `tour[]` and `complexity`.

findings.title: Corrections and measurements could not be verified from this checkout
findings.description: This checkout has no `commands/analysis/understand.md`, no `.understand-anything/` graph and no 943 sample, and 361's design and tasks are both `not_started`. The 361 design does not contain either corrected claim; it already says `select(.type == "file" or ...)`. So the corrections target the skill text, not the design. Walkthrough step 1 re-measures and stops on disagreement, which is adequate.

findings.title: Small cuts and wording
findings.description:
- **Unused field:** `edges[].direction` is listed as consumed (line 86) but no section uses it.
- **`languageNotes`:** the annotation (lines 209-212) is the design's one self-made exception to the no-silent-omission rule and nothing requires it; consider cutting it.
- **"Unchanged" wording:** the "Read discipline, unchanged" heading sits over a widened filter. "Retain the document unchanged" (line 258) sits beside an added cross-reference line.
- **Confusing parenthetical:** line 234 describes an all-comments file while citing 17 active lines.
